hints.title: Excluding Representative Ties
hints.text: Sales representatives who booked orders linked to a specified vendor must be excluded entirely from the final roster.

hints.title: Anti-Join Subquery Formulation
hints.text: Join Orders with Company to find all sales_id linked to the company named Red. Then filter SalesPerson with sales_id not in that list.

hints.title: Not In Subquery Blueprint
hints.text: Select name from SalesPerson where sales_id not in (select o.sales_id from Orders o join Company c on o.com_id = c.com_id where c.name = 'Red').

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT name
FROM SalesPerson
WHERE sales_id NOT IN (
    SELECT o.sales_id
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN Company c ON o.com_id = c.com_id
    WHERE c.name = 'RED'
);
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Filtering orders with company name != RED erroneously retains salespersons who also took RED orders on different dates.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Subquery collects distinct seller identifiers who dealt with RED and eliminates them via anti-join.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding that someone can have orders with RED and other companies simultaneously.

    WHERE c.name = 'RED'

import pandas as pd

def sales_person(sales_person: pd.DataFrame, company: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    red_companies = company[company['name'] == 'RED']['com_id']
    red_sales_ids = orders[orders['com_id'].isin(red_companies)]['sales_id'].unique()
    result = sales_person[~sales_person['sales_id'].isin(red_sales_ids)]
    return result[['name']]
